::: {#thm-same-value}
#### Having the same value is an equivalence relation

Let $f : A \to B$ be a function (@def-function),
and on $A$ let $a \sim a'$ when $f(a) = f(a')$.
Then $\sim$ is an equivalence relation (@def-equivalence-relation).

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

The steps of @exm-same-length work for any function in place of $\operatorname{len}$.

**Reflexive.**
For each $a \in A$, $f(a) = f(a)$, so $a \sim a$.

**Symmetric.**
If $a \sim a'$, then $f(a) = f(a')$, so $f(a') = f(a)$, and $a' \sim a$.

**Transitive.**
If $a \sim a'$ and $a' \sim a''$, then $f(a) = f(a')$ and $f(a') = f(a'')$,
so $f(a) = f(a'')$ (@thm-equal-trans), and $a \sim a''$.

:::

:::
